TODAY — recreated from shared/report-deck-view.tsx + report-deck-styles.ts, so the comparison is fair. Click through it.

What it costs you:
· Two decks behind one switcher, and slide 1 of each is the SAME Review brief.
· A facts sidebar takes ~28% of the brief and pins the prose column at 74ch on a 1440px surface.
· Findings and change map paginate into "part 1 / 2" — you page rather than scan, and the footnote under three rows still reads "9 of 9 files".
· Guidance — the one section that tells you what to do — is slide 3 of 5, buried between facts and file lists.

A — REFINEMENT. Same content, same components, better spine.

· The footer step strip becomes a persistent left rail, so you see the whole briefing's shape before you walk it.
· One briefing, not two decks — the overview/issues switcher and the duplicated brief slide both disappear.
· Order is BRIEF → FOR YOU → EVIDENCE. Guidance outranks raw facts.
· Facts move to a strip above the brief so the prose gets full width.
· Sections scroll; no more "part 1 / 2".
· Draft comments vs report-only notes are finally labelled as different things.

Tradeoff: still a document you read. It does not help you act.

B — RETHOUGHT. The briefing stops being a presentation and becomes a worklist.

· Brief stays, as the lede — kept whole.
· Everything else becomes one triage queue: severity-ordered decisions, each expandable, each with open-in-diff / edit comment / dismiss.
· The sidebar is now only WHY I'M UNSURE — the risks that drive the verdict — plus a handoff to the workbench chat. The checklist and the what-I-checked roll-up are gone: both restated things the queue and the brief already said.
· Progress is "2 of 4 cleared", not "slide 3 of 7".
· Change map demotes to context behind the EVERYTHING filter.
· It ends on the real next step: open the workbench and submit.

Tradeoff: further from the current code, and it presumes triage state the review record does not store yet.

All three are the Reviews-panel overlay at 1440×920 (its real max size), dark theme, in the shipped neondeck system — Chakra Petch / IBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Mono, square borders, #00b7c7 primary on #0a0b10.

Use the theme tweak above each artboard to check the light palette.

Sample data is a composite: the real files and churn from #315, with plausible findings in the same subsystem. A and B both lift --panel one step off --canvas so the frame reads as a surface rather than a hairline — in dark theme today they resolve to the same #0a0b10.

B · RECOMMEND APPROVE — sample PR #314.

TWO verdicts, not three: approve, or needs a human. That is the real decision — can this merge without a human reading the diff.

· Nothing to triage, so the findings are a MANIFEST of what is about to be sent: same card and same three verbs as the needs-a-human board, rendered compact.
· The button states its whole payload, verdict and comment count together. Never a bare "Approve".
· "+ add a note with your approval" is the HUMAN's, written by you, posting as the review body. Neon does not draft it — an agent asked whether anything is worth flagging will find something every time, and that noise would go out under your name.
· Press Approve: the briefing becomes a receipt rather than closing. No undo, and the footer says so.

The sidebar's one "double-check this" item comes from overview.risks, which can legitimately be empty. It stays inside the briefing and never enters the published review — say the word if you think it has the same bias problem.

B · NEEDS A HUMAN — sample PR #315, the same one on the Directions page.

Same layout, different defaults. Verdict bar turns, filter defaults to BLOCKERS, blockers open expanded, sidebar leads with WHY I'M ESCALATING.

· The brief answers a different question: not "why is this safe" but "what makes this hard". Same slot, same length, different job — that is a prompt change in pr-review-prompts.ts, not just a UI one.
· Card actions are open in diff / edit comment / dismiss. Edit opens the draft in place; dismiss is the only thing that changes state, so the two are no longer ambiguous.
· Approve is NOT hidden. A de-emphasized "Approve anyway" opens an acknowledgement band naming what you are overriding — and carrying the note field, because approving over a recommendation is exactly when you want to say why.
· Chat is deliberately absent: the sidebar routes to the workbench instead.

REVIEWS PANEL — the surface that matters most if the verdicts are any good.

Built on the shipped panel: same section headers (bg-field, 10px mono, right-aligned count), same row anatomy, same Badge and Button.

· Two verdicts on the rows, each with its one-line reason. Approve one and the row becomes a receipt without the briefing ever opening.
· The two report buttons (overview / issues) collapse into one "briefing".
· A needs-a-human row has no approve button at all. The override exists, but inside the briefing next to the reasoning, not out here where it would be a reflex.

If this works the briefing gets less traffic, not more. Worth designing for on purpose.
